ielts_reading_sets.title: Urban Greening Initiatives
ielts_reading_sets.description: An article exploring how cities integrate vegetation to improve living standards and ecological stability.

ielts_reading_sets.title: Adaptive Learning Platforms
ielts_reading_sets.description: A report discussing data-driven educational platforms and their impact on student progress monitoring.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Some cities in the passage saw green roofs primarily as decorative projects.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The passage states that early adopters viewed green roofs as experimental solutions to insulation and drainage, not decoration.

ielts_reading_questions.body: European regulations compelled all large commercial buildings to install rooftop gardens.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The text mentions incentives in parts of Europe but no universal regulation or requirement for all large buildings.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Residents in coastal districts opposed the creation of bioswales because they reduced parking space.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The article describes resistance in coastal districts where bioswales replaced roadside parking, leading to initial opposition.

ielts_reading_questions.body: According to the passage, what feature allowed the city of Norham to reduce flood insurance premiums?
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Norham’s transport authority embedded permeable materials beneath tram tracks, which improved drainage and convinced insurers to lower premiums.

ielts_reading_questions.body: What data did Vellan City collect to justify expanding tree canopies?
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Vellan City monitored household electricity use during summer and linked reduced consumption to streets with dense tree cover.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Match each city with the primary challenge it faced when implementing greening projects.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Harwick lacked trained installers, Norham struggled to keep systems funded once grants ended, and Lazaro needed special permits to modify heritage facades.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Which benefit of community orchards is highlighted in the passage?
options: They shorten food supply chains by exporting fruit abroad.
They provide seasonal meeting spaces that strengthen neighbourhood ties.
They double the biodiversity of existing parks within one year.
They eliminate the need for city-funded composting services.
ielts_reading_questions.correct_answer: They provide seasonal meeting spaces that strengthen neighbourhood ties.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The text emphasises how orchard harvest days drew residents together, enhancing social cohesion.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Why did the transport department trial vertical gardens on noise barriers?
options: To comply with new wildlife protection legislation
To disguise concrete walls near tourist areas
To test whether vegetation could absorb traffic pollution
ielts_reading_questions.correct_answer: To test whether vegetation could absorb traffic pollution
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The department installed vertical gardens on sound barriers to see if plants could capture fine particulates from congested roads.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Pilot schools abandoned traditional grades entirely when adopting adaptive platforms.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The report notes that schools combined adaptive feedback with existing grade books rather than discarding grades.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Teachers initially worried that adaptive software would limit their autonomy.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Early interviews revealed concern that algorithm-generated lesson paths might override teacher judgement.

ielts_reading_questions.body: The platform delivered identical question banks to all learners.
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: It specifically customises question banks based on the learner’s speed and accuracy data.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Which subject saw the fastest improvement during the second term of the trial?
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The report indicates that mathematics classes experienced measurable progress earlier than literacy classes.

ielts_reading_questions.body: What two metrics did the analytics dashboard display for each student?
ielts_reading_questions.correct_answer: time on task and mastery probability
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Teachers monitored how long students spent on activities and the system’s prediction of mastery for each objective.

ielts_reading_questions.body: According to the passage, what persuaded administrators to continue funding the platform?
options: Parents volunteered to cover licensing costs
The vendor offered lifetime access for a single payment
Benchmark exams showed gains among previously underperforming pupils
The platform integrated with the city’s public transport cards
ielts_reading_questions.correct_answer: Benchmark exams showed gains among previously underperforming pupils
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Administrators renewed the programme after seeing a significant rise in benchmark scores for students below level.

ielts_reading_questions.body: Match each stakeholder with their primary concern or benefit.
correct_answer: Parents: needing transparency on data privacy
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: The passage highlights students’ desire for instant hints, teachers’ request for workload forecasts, and parents’ questions about data storage.

ielts_reading_questions.body: What challenge delayed the platform’s expansion to rural campuses?
ielts_reading_questions.explanation: Rural schools lacked stable broadband, making it difficult to synchronise data in real time.

ielts_listening_sets.title: Coastal Research Internship Briefing
ielts_listening_sets.description: A university coordinator explains internship logistics, followed by a returning student sharing fieldwork experiences.
ielts_listening_sets.audio_script: [Coordinator] Good morning everyone. Before you register for the coastal research internship, let me outline the essentials. Applications close on the fifteenth of May, so please have your forms and supervisor signatures ready a week earlier for checks. Only second- and third-year students with at least one lab course completed may apply. The university pays for your return ferry ticket to Silverstrand Island, but you must arrange your own train fare to the harbour. Accommodation is provided in converted lighthouse quarters, which sleep six per room. They are basic but include lockers, showers and a shared workspace. Before you travel, you must attend the on-campus first-aid workshop on the 22nd of April; it is compulsory because we work on slippery jetties. During the five-week placement, Mondays are reserved for drone mapping, Wednesdays for water sampling, and Fridays for community presentations in the village hall. Pack sturdy boots, a waterproof jacket and especially a headlamp, as the island paths have no lighting after sunset. Finally, on the first weekend you will meet local fishers to record oral histories about shoreline change, so prepare respectful interview questions. [Student] Hi everyone, I’m Lia, and I joined last year’s team. The work is rewarding but be ready for surprises. For example, heavy fog settled over the island during our second week, so we had to postpone drone flights until the sky cleared. Instead, we focused on cataloguing specimens indoors. The science tasks are manageable, yet uploading files can be frustrating because the satellite internet is slow; I often stayed up late waiting for tide data to sync. My advice is to take neat field notes so you can catch up on data entry when the connection improves. The local community is welcoming, and the fishers will happily share stories if you show patience.

ielts_listening_questions.body: What is the application deadline mentioned by the coordinator?
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: The coordinator states that applications must be submitted by the 15th of May.

ielts_listening_questions.body: Which skill workshop is mandatory before departure?
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: All interns must complete a campus-based first aid course as stated in the briefing.

ielts_listening_questions.body: Which transport cost is covered by the university?
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: The coordinator explains that the university pays for the return ferry ticket to the research island.

ielts_listening_questions.body: How are students accommodated on the island?
options: Guest rooms at the marine college
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: The briefing specifies that interns stay in dormitories inside a renovated lighthouse complex.

ielts_listening_questions.body: Which weather condition forced last year’s team to pause surveys?
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: The returning student recalls a week of heavy fog that halted drone-based coastline surveys.

ielts_listening_questions.body: What did the returning student find most challenging about data entry?
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: She states that the unstable satellite link made file uploads frustrating.

ielts_listening_questions.body: Match each task with the day of the week it is scheduled.
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: The coordinator outlines the weekly cycle: mapping on Monday, sampling mid-week, and presentations to residents on Friday afternoons.

ielts_listening_questions.body: What item does the coordinator advise students to bring for evening field walks?
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: She emphasises packing a headlamp because paths lack lighting after sunset.

ielts_listening_questions.body: Why will interns meet local fishers on their first weekend?
options: To collect oral histories of shoreline change
ielts_listening_questions.correct_answer: To collect oral histories of shoreline change
ielts_listening_questions.explanation: Students conduct interviews with fishers to gather qualitative data about erosion patterns.

ielts_writing_tasks.title: Changes in Urban Transport Preferences
ielts_writing_tasks.prompt: The charts below show the percentage of commuters using four modes of transport (metro, bus, cycling, ride-sharing) in a European city in 2000, 2010 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

ielts_writing_tasks.title: Process Diagram: Water Recycling Factory
ielts_writing_tasks.prompt: The diagram illustrates how a factory collects, filters, and reuses wastewater for industrial cooling. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
ielts_writing_tasks.sample_answer:
The diagram depicts a closed-loop system through which a factory captures wastewater and recycles it for cooling machinery. Overall, the process features three stages: collection and storage, mechanical and chemical treatment, and redistribution to the cooling units.

First, wastewater from manufacturing lines flows through floor drains into a covered reservoir. A set of coarse grates removes large debris before water enters the reservoir. From there, pumps move the liquid into a primary filtration chamber that contains sand and gravel layers. Suspended particles settle to the bottom while a conveyor extracts sludge for external disposal.

The partially cleaned water proceeds to a chemical treatment tank where it is aerated and exposed to ultraviolet lamps. A measured quantity of neutralising solution is added to balance the pH. Once sensors confirm that the water meets safety standards, it is transferred to an elevated storage tower. Finally, gravity feeds the recycled water back into the cooling jackets surrounding heavy machinery. After absorbing heat, the water returns to the drains, and the cycle begins again.

ielts_writing_tasks.title: Remote Work and Urban Centres
ielts_writing_tasks.prompt: More employees now work from home at least part of the week. Some people believe this trend will revitalise smaller towns, while others think it will weaken city economies. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
ielts_writing_tasks.sample_answer:
The rise of remote work has triggered debates about its impact on urban centres. While many argue that flexible work arrangements will breathe new life into smaller towns, others worry that large cities will suffer economically. In my view, the most likely outcome is a partial redistribution of activity rather than a dramatic decline in urban economies.

Supporters of remote work point out that employees are no longer tied to city offices. When people move to smaller towns, they bring purchasing power and fresh demand for services, which can stimulate local shops, co-working hubs and cultural venues. Furthermore, remote professionals can volunteer their skills in regional schools or start-ups, diversifying local labour markets.

However, opponents claim that when commuters stay home, metropolitan businesses such as cafes, transport operators and retail outlets lose revenue. This concern is valid in the short term, especially for neighbourhoods that depend on office workers. Yet major cities have historically adapted by reinventing their use of space, converting older office towers into housing or labs, and attracting new industries such as green tech or media production.

Overall, remote work does not necessarily spell decline for city economies. Instead, it encourages both urban and rural areas to innovate. Policymakers should facilitate this transition by improving broadband infrastructure nationwide and redesigning city centres to support mixed-use developments.
